title: The Stuff You Should Know 2015 Jolly Christmas Extravaganza
summary: Josh and Chuck's annual Christmas holiday episode, a holiday extravaganza tour of Christmas traditions. Segments cover unusual Christmas customs in India, Japan (KFC Christmas tradition), Finland (cemetery candles, bed left open for ancestors, sauna), Venezuela (string tied to toe, roller skaters), and Sweden (the Gävle Christmas goat burnings). Then the history of department store Christmas window displays (Macy's, Lord & Taylor, Woodward & Lothrop penguins), the history of fruitcake and its Christmas baking traditions, sugar plums that contain no plums, gingerbread history including Katharina Schraderin, and oranges in stockings. Next, trivia about the movie Elf (script, stop-motion styling, Jack-in-the-box scene, Maurice LaMarche burp, Will Ferrell as a department store Santa, sequel offer). The episode closes with a reading of the 1897 New York Sun "Yes, Virginia, there is a Santa Claus" letter and reply, plus holiday sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and holiday greetings
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck welcome listeners to the 2015 holiday episode, joke about the studio air conditioning, mention the Christmas blog post collection, and encourage a family fireside holiday with cold duck and other drinks.

segments.title: Christmas customs around the world
segments.summary: A tour of unusual Christmas traditions: India uses mango and orange tree leaves as decorations; Japan's KFC Christmas Eve dinner tradition started around 1974 with a Kentucky Fried Chicken campaign; Finland families light candles at ancestors' graves and leave beds and saunas open for the dead; in Caracas, Venezuela, children tie strings to their toes so roller skaters on the way to early Mass can tug them awake; and in Gävle, Sweden, a straw Yule goat is erected each year and is often burned by vandals despite fireproofing.

segments.title: Department store Christmas window displays
segments.summary: Chuck recalls visiting New York holiday windows. The history traces back to plate glass windows during the Industrial Revolution, Roland Hussey Macy's store and early Christmas displays and in-store Santa, the 1874 porcelain doll and Uncle Tom's Cabin scene, electric lighting, Lord & Taylor's moving bell displays, Neiman Marcus's frosted trees, live penguins at Woodward & Lothrop, and artists involved in window design.

segments.title: Fruitcake history and Christmas sweets
segments.summary: The hosts discuss fruitcake's reputation and the Manitou Springs Great Fruitcake Toss, then trace its origins to ancient Rome and Middle Eastern spiced cakes, its European spread and baking, and the Claxton, Georgia and Corsicana, Texas bakeries. They then explain that sugar plums are candies with no plums, that plum pudding has no plums either, and give gingerbread history including Katharina Schraderin, and the tradition of oranges in stockings.

segments.title: Trivia about the movie Elf
segments.summary: Facts about the 2003 film Elf: the script was originally written with Jim Carrey in mind, the film used stop-motion-inspired look and Rudolph-style elf costumes, Ray Harryhausen appears as a voice for a polar bear cub, the Jack-in-the-box scene reactions were genuine, Maurice LaMarche provided the burp, Will Ferrell and Chris Kattan both worked as department store Santa and elf before SNL, and Ferrell turned down a sequel offer.

segments.title: Christmas reading: Yes, Virginia, there is a Santa Claus
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read the 1897 letter from Virginia O'Hanlon to the New York Sun asking whether Santa Claus is real, and the editors' famous reply affirming his existence and the importance of faith and imagination.
topics: Yes Virginia there is a Santa Claus

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank staff and listeners, wish everyone a merry Christmas and happy holidays, and sign off.
